test_title: PYST 45: SSC GD Constable - English (Held On - 20 Feb, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

His first movement after the shock ________ to work in his loom; and he went on with this unremittingly.
solution:
The correct answer is **option 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This is a compound sentence and there are two verbs in this sentence named **'had been'(BE**) and **'went'.**
 
• "he **went **on with this unremittingly" in this part of the sentence we find '**went' **is the past indefinite form of verb **'Go**'. So the tense of the entire sentence is in past. 
 
• Two verbs with their past indefinite form **can not co-exist together **in a same sentence. Because two facts can not happen at the same time. For example-
 
 
• The patient **had died **before the doctor** came.**
 
• The school prayer **had started** before I** reached.**
 
 
 
• So while there are two main verbs present in a sentence in **past tense**, one of the verbs must be placed in its **past participle form (V3)** in order to justify its action earlier than the other verb present there.
 
• Two main verbs in this sentence are '**be'** and '**go'.** Since '**went' **is in past indefinite form , **'be'** verb should be placed in its** past participle** form . So the correct answer is '**had been'.​**

​Therefore, the correct statement is **His first movement after the shock had been to work in his loom; and he went on with this unremittingly. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The 1st option is **incorrect** as '**was been**' is the past indefinite form of verb '**be' **and it is in **passive voice.** That doesn't signify the meaning of the sentence.
 
• The 2nd option is** incorrect **as '**has being**' is an incorrect structure of tense. As** V3** is to be placed after **have/has/had,** but here being is a** V4 **form of '**be**' verb. Moreover '**has' **is present form so it doesn't go with another verb which is in** past** in the same sentence. 
 
• Option 4 is **incorrect** as **'have been'** is signifies** present** tense of the **action/verb**. So it can not be used having another verb in **past tense** in the same sentence. 

2f
